title: RWB-S8-E7002-APP: the X2 slice has no plan row for its four consumed contracts, its outbox library, its EFS touch, its requirement ids, its work-management owners or its screen read
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.6, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E7002-APP; context pack S8 rwb-deviation (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 8 and 13); legacy RWB-E7-002; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.3, A2.4, A2.11, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.2, T4, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01, R-DEV-03, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-17 and R-DEV-20; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-DVF-02
description: (1) The plan gives H = RWB-S8-E7002-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the step reads the rwb-case case facts, answers the rwb-case case move, reads the rwb-source-data data product and reads the rwb-decision package, so four consumed rows have no plan row. (2) DP-09 (outbox and inbox) is absent although the service owns topic rwb.deviation.events.v1 with events EV-06 and EV-07, so the library row RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is absent from the H row. (3) DP-04 is absent although the step evaluates R-DEV-03, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-17 and R-DEV-20 of a route set of 22 rules over 9 states, so no kit row RWB-PLT-E1072-CON or C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is held. (4) FSD S8 A2.11 and the Epics 3 to 8 Specification row FEAT-DVF-02 name EFS as an integration point, the plan's X row is empty and the connection matrix gives S8 no external cell, so no source says how the EFS touch is carried. (5) Legacy AC2 tests R-DEV-17, which the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives to X6 contact-not-found, while the feature runs X2 whose own path is R-DEV-03 and R-DEV-10. (6) The plan carries no requirement id for this key, while FSD S8 Requirements served gives REQ-S8-002, REQ-DVH-005 and REQ-S8-004. (7) The legacy Data table names queue, assignment and timer, which no ownership row of S8 assigns to a service. (8) The legacy permission table gives Case record U to eight named roles and 4 more, and the four are not named. (9) The Ownership Map gives rwb-deviation two operations and no deviation read, so the read SCR-08 needs has no operation. (10) The plan keeps wave 4 for EP07 while the service's Arch v5 wave is 2; R5.6 states only the earlier-W-MAP case. (11) No source ties the identifiers EV-06 and EV-07 to the names DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared of TSD S8 T5.3.
evidence: split plan slice RWB-S8-E7002-APP with three H rows and empty C, I and X; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04, DP-05, DP-09 and DP-16 rows and R5.6; context pack ownership rows of S8 (table deviation, two REST operations, events EV-06 and EV-07, no job, workflow DeviationWorkflow) and connection-matrix row S8 (REST and events to P1, Temporal and events to P10, events from P3); FSD S8 A2.11.2 (integration points Workbench, EFS) and Requirements served; TSD S8 T3.1, T4, T5.3 and T6.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-03, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-17 and R-DEV-20; legacy RWB-E7-002 Data, Endpoints, Permission checks, Acceptance criteria and Test cases
proposed: Keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows as they stand; record the four consumed rows as class C in fact with their placeholders; record RWB-PLT-TE006-CON as the wave 0 library the topic needs and RWB-PLT-E1072-CON with RWB-P7-E1073-CON as the kit the evaluation needs; confirm how the EFS touch is carried and whether rwb-integration owns it; adopt REQ-S8-002, REQ-DVH-005 and REQ-S8-004 from the FSD; confirm the owner of queue, assignment and timer and the four unnamed roles; confirm the deviation read SCR-08 needs with the Ownership Map owner; confirm the EV-06 and EV-07 names

title: RWB-S8-E7002-CON: the deviation element, the four consumed operation names, the event names, the two shared operations, the deviating read and the field-level types have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E7002-CON; context pack S8 rwb-deviation; legacy RWB-E7-002; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.2, A2.4, A2.5, A2.11, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01, R-DEV-03, R-DEV-10, R-DEV-17 and R-DEV-20
description: (1) The rwb-case case read and move answer, the rwb-source-data data-product read and the rwb-decision package read publish no operation name, so all four consumed rows carry a placeholder, and the consumed case event has no name. (2) TSD S8 T5.3 names the service two published events and no source ties the identifiers EV-06 and EV-07 to those names or publishes an AsyncAPI catalogue. (3) The Ownership Map gives rwb-deviation exactly two operations and the legacy key lists both, while the Epic 2 raise story and the sibling X keys of the same service list the same two, so no source says which story owns the declaration. (4) The deviation read SCR-08 needs is in no operation inventory. (5) TSD S8 T-A.2 gives the error set as status codes with no message id per condition, so each condition is bound to a message of the legacy and FSD set. (6) The plan's C, I and X rows are empty while the baseline declares four consumed rows, two published events and one consumed event. (7) FSD S8 A2.11 names EFS as an integration point of the feature and the plan carries no X row.
evidence: TSD S8 T-A.1 operations API-S8-001 and API-S8-002 only, and T-A.2 error lists 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 without message ids; TSD S8 T5.3 two published events without identifiers; context pack ownership rows of S8 (two REST operations, events EV-06 and EV-07) and connection-matrix row S8; FSD S8 A2.11.4.4 (no background event) and Screens SCR-06 and SCR-08; legacy RWB-E7-002 Endpoints and messages MSG-S8-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003
proposed: Publish the baseline with the placeholders, bind every error condition to one message id of section 14, declare the deviation element with its ten columns and three lists, declare the two shared operations once for the service and have the Epic 2 raise story and the sibling X keys reference them, confirm the four operation names and the consumed event name with their owners before the tag, confirm the EV-06 and EV-07 names, and record the tag date in the contract README
